mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened discount rates eroding equity present value.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of such triggered periods, or FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5% for the next 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.0% for three consecutive months, labor market slack increases, boosting consumer confidence and driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such episodes, or other labor indicators (PAYEMS) show no significant change.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in HOUST (household spending index) above 2% for two months predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as anticipated consumption growth supports equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 2% growth for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >40% of triggered windows, or INDPRO shows contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in >60% of such events, or other supply indicators (GDPC1) show expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month for three months, the expectation of higher inflation leads to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return via rate path uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly % change > 0.5 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of such episodes, or FEDFUNDS rises by <0.1% over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in PAYEMS (employment) and UNRATE (unemployment) by at least 0.5 percentage points each month for two months signals a tight labor market, pushing 60-day S&P 500 forward returns positive.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change <= -0.5% AND UNRATE monthly change <= -0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >40% of such triggered windows, or other demand indicators (GDPC1) show no change.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 4% monthly increase in GDPC1 (GDP) for three months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong demand supports equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change > 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of such episodes, or other demand proxies (HOUST) show muted growth.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 10% for two consecutive months during a low-inflation regime, S&P 500 60-day forward returns turn negative due to weak consumer demand signals.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -10% for two consecutive months AND regime: inflation < 2%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of such events, or other demand indicators (HOUST) show no decline.
